name: Quran learning
title: Free Quran Puzzles, Maps & Study Tools | Moongazer
heading: Five ways to spend time with the Quran
description: Trace themes across passages, explore parables and places, and read prophet accounts and revelation context with Pickthall translations and sources right beside the text.
intro: Whether you have ten minutes for a daily theme puzzle or longer to sit with a parable, these five tools meet you where you are. Pick a puzzle when you want a quick challenge, a map when you want to place a name, or a guided reading when you want to slow down with commentary.
guidance: Start with the verses themselves before opening any note or diagram. Pickthall translations and classical commentary are always kept clearly separate from our questions and visual aids, so you can see where the scripture ends and the study tool begins.

questions.question: Which translation do these tools use?
questions.answer: Quoted English Quran passages use Marmaduke Pickthall's translation, with verse references and source notes linked on each page.

questions.question: Where can I explore diagrams or places?
questions.answer: Parables of the Quran pairs each passage with a simple visual map of its imagery, while Places in the Quran links verses to geography and leaves uncertain sites unpinned on the map.

name: Seerah & history
title: Seerah & Islamic History Explorers | Moongazer
heading: Read Seerah and Islamic history with the sources open
description: Trace the Prophet's life ﷺ year by year, weigh primary reports in short cases, and follow Islamic civilization across nine regions from 661 to 1648 CE.
intro: Good history starts by looking closely at what the sources actually say. Follow the major turns of the Prophet's life ﷺ on a timeline, step into a short Seerah case to test what a report establishes, or zoom out across ten centuries of cities, trade, and scholarship.
guidance: Not every historical date carries the same certainty. Where a year is conventional or approximate, the notes say so plainly—and when two events sit near each other on a timeline, we keep their context separate unless the sources link them directly.

items.reason: Browse a sourced chronology, then open an event to read the reports and date notes.

items.label: Which came first? (Seerah Timeline)
items.reason: Arrange four events from the prophetic mission, then compare their sources and approximate dates.

questions.question: Are these complete history courses?
questions.answer: No. They are selected reading tools. The Seerah timeline and the common-claims checks focus on particular events and questions, while the civilization timeline presents twenty-four selected records across nine regions.

questions.question: What should I check before treating a date as exact?
questions.answer: Read the individual event's dating and source notes. A report may support an event without giving its displayed calendar year. The tools retain that distinction rather than making every record appear equally precise.

name: Prayer & everyday practice
title: Hifz Planning, Zakat & Everyday Akhlaq | Moongazer
heading: Bring what you learn into study and daily life
description: Plan a realistic hifz and revision routine, calculate zakat step by step, and think through everyday character dilemmas.
intro: Knowledge settles when it meets daily habit. Map out a hifz schedule that protects your revision first, work through a real-world akhlaq dilemma, or calculate your zakat with every scholarly option clearly labelled.
guidance: Use these tools as practical companions, not verdicts. The hifz planner estimates time based on your own pace, the akhlaq scenarios are conversation starters rather than rulings, and the zakat calculator shows its working so you can verify complex questions with a scholar.

items.reason: Weigh what selected historical reports actually establish before drawing a conclusion.

questions.question: Does the Zakat Calculator issue a religious ruling?
questions.answer: No. It shows the working for common scholarly options with source notes so you can verify complex or unusual holdings with a qualified scholar.

questions.question: Can I use the business cases as a ruling on my transaction?
questions.answer: No. The business scenarios in Everyday Akhlaq present fictional educational cases. Real arrangements can involve facts and obligations outside an exercise, so the app does not certify transactions or provide personalized legal or financial advice.

name: Games & family activities
title: Quran Escape Rooms, Seerah Challenges & Family Halaqa | Moongazer
heading: Play together, then open the passage
description: Solve Quran escape rooms, race a Seerah chronology, or sit down for a ten-minute family halaqa.
intro: Learning sticks better when people are talking and thinking together. Gather around one screen for a Quran escape room, test your sense of chronology in Seerah Timeline, or pick a ten-minute Family Halaqa pack with a verse, a question, and a shared activity.
guidance: Every game here runs straight in the browser with no sign-ups, leaderboards, or profiles. Read the clues aloud, adapt the wording for younger kids, and treat the score as a light prompt to open the verses afterward.

questions.question: Are these synchronized multiplayer games?
questions.answer: No. They run in the browser on the device being used. People can discuss an escape room or family activity together on one screen; the collection does not create a live multiplayer session or player accounts.

questions.question: How should I choose an activity for children?
questions.answer: Family Halaqa includes suggested age bands and times. An adult can read aloud, adapt vocabulary and let participants pass. Keep discussion examples fictional and choose a pack that suits the group rather than treating the age label as a strict requirement.
